books.title: The Last Dragon Egg
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: High in the mountains, in a cave of warm stones, lay the last dragon egg in the world. It had been waiting a hundred years to hatch.
A shepherd boy called Tomas found the cave while looking for a lost lamb. 'What a strange stone,' he thought, until the egg moved.
Tomas carried the egg home and kept it warm by the fire. He read to it every night, telling it stories of the world outside.
One spring morning, the egg cracked. Out came a tiny dragon with emerald scales and eyes like gold coins. 'Hello, little one,' whispered Tomas.
The dragon grew quickly, and Tomas taught it to fly, to fish in the mountain lakes, and to sing with the birds at dawn.
When the dragon was fully grown, it spread its great wings and flew in a circle around the mountain, breathing a rainbow of fire into the sky.
Tomas watched it soar away, and though he was sad, he was glad too. The last dragon was free, and the world had magic in it once more.

books.title: The Star Collector
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Every night, an old man called Elias climbed to the top of his hill with a glass jar, to collect the stars that fell from the sky.
He kept each fallen star in a jar on his windowsill, and on dark nights their gentle light lit up the whole village.
One evening, a little girl called Pia followed him up the hill. 'Why do you collect the stars?' she asked.
'Because every star has a wish inside it,' said Elias, 'and a wish should never be wasted.'
That night, a bright star fell right at Pia's feet. Elias picked it up carefully and handed it to her. 'This one is yours,' he said. 'Make a wish.'
Pia closed her eyes and wished that her grandmother, who was ill, would feel better. The star glowed warmly in her hands.
The next morning, her grandmother was sitting up in bed, smiling and asking for breakfast. Pia ran to thank Elias, but he only smiled and said, 'The stars heard you.'

books.title: The House on the Hill
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: On the top of the hill stood an empty house with blue shutters and a garden full of wild roses. Nobody had lived there for years.
When the Alvarez family moved to the village, they bought the house. The children, Diego and Lucia, were excited — and a little bit nervous.
'It is just a house,' said their mother. 'We will make it a home.' So they cleaned, painted, and planted flowers in the garden.
One rainy afternoon, Diego found a box in the attic. Inside were letters, photographs, and a map of the village from long ago.
The letters told the story of the family who had lived there before them, and the map showed a hidden well in the garden, long forgotten.
The Alvarez family cleared the well and planted a rose bush beside it, in memory of the family who had loved the house before them.
Now the house on the hill is full of laughter, light, and the smell of fresh bread, and everyone in the village says it is the happiest house of all.

books.title: The Girl Who Chased the Wind
books.author: Yently Kids
pages: Nora was a girl who loved the wind. She ran after it through fields and over hills, trying to catch it in her hands, but the wind always slipped away, laughing.
"Why do you chase me?" the wind asked one day, swirling around her. "Because I want to know where you go," Nora replied. "Take me with you."
The wind lifted Nora gently into the air. They flew over green valleys, across wide oceans, and above snowy mountains. Nora saw deserts, forests, and cities she had never imagined.
At last, the wind set her down in a field of golden wheat. "The wind never stays in one place," it whispered, "but it always comes back to those who love it."
Nora walked home with the wind playing in her hair. She knew she would never catch the wind, but she would chase it forever — and that was enough.
